summary: The fix-range classification keeps only runtimeLines and errors and throws away range.class. A fix that deletes a test (or code) file added earlier on the branch is gate-class in the range but invisible to the whole-branch diff and the gate scan, so the plan picks the scoped pass and skips the specialists. The docs promise that a fix touching a gate-class path keeps the full pass 2.
evidence: Scratch repo: feat adds src/b.ts and test/b.test.ts; the fix commit runs `git rm test/b.test.ts` and appends a line to src/b.ts. `gstack-review-plan --base main --pass 1 --last full --fixed-blocking --range-base <pass head>` (real gate scan) printed GATE_SCAN: tagged=0, FIX_RANGE: runtime_lines=1, NEXT: scoped (fix-check, <reader>, adversarial, <reader> only). classifyDiff on collectCommit(<pass head>, HEAD) returned {"class":"gate","reasons":["tests: test/b.test.ts","deletes 1 code or test path(s)"],"runtimeLines":0}. The CLI never checks range.class, and nextStep only sees rangeRuntimeLines.

summary: In a scoped pass, the skipped-reviewers note about unforced specialists is tied to the <reader> branch. It is missing whenever the <reader> is dispatched, and it claims specialists were skipped even when a forced specialist was dispatched.
evidence: `if (stepElevenPending) add('<reader>', ...); else if (numbersChanged) add(...); else skipped.push('specialists and <reader> (scoped pass)');`. With adversarialRan=false and class=code, the usual pass-2 case, no SKIP line names the specialists the scoped pass left out.
